source_note: Synthetic abbreviated evidence inspired by the five KPMG examples; not verified paper excerpts, model output or unseen evaluation. Runtime never reads this file.

cases.evidence: The three-part workflow collected survey responses, organized the data and predicted travel demand in a small student sample.

implications.text: The three-part workflow connected survey collection, data organization and travel prediction in a small student sample. This could inform clearer handoffs in advisory survey analysis.
implications.suggested_action: Map the survey collection and analysis handoffs to the studied stages; document inputs, outputs and review responsibilities before deciding which stage merits automation.
assumptions: Transfer to the proposed workflow remains untested.

limitations: Transfer gap: a small student sample does not establish performance for client populations.

cases.evidence: Workflow reconstruction from computer-use traces preserved task switches that a standard process summary omitted.

implications.text: Workflow reconstruction preserved task switches omitted by a standard summary. This could reveal missing onboarding handoffs in process documentation.
implications.suggested_action: Ask process owners to compare reconstructed task switches with documented onboarding handoffs and record missing steps.
assumptions: Transfer to the proposed workflow remains untested.

risks: Potential concern: collecting onboarding screen traces could expose sensitive information; consent and data minimization need review.
limitations: Transfer gap: the observed traces do not establish onboarding performance.

cases.evidence: The routing method used a low-cost estimate and reserved expensive model checks for decisions where more information was valuable.

implications.text: The routing method reserved expensive model checks for decisions where more information was valuable. This could inform model-selection rules for document classification without establishing cost savings.
implications.suggested_action: Compare the routing method with fixed model selection on representative document classification cases; measure answer quality, request cost and latency to decide when extra checks are justified.
assumptions: Transfer to the proposed workflow remains untested.

limitations: Transfer gap: the routing result does not establish savings or suitable rules for this workflow.

cases.evidence: Coding agents mainly changed training settings rather than learning methods; meaningful algorithmic improvement remained limited.

implications.text: Coding agents mainly changed training settings rather than learning methods. This could help reviewers distinguish configuration changes from claimed algorithmic improvements.
implications.suggested_action: Ask the technical team to classify each claimed training improvement and rerun the changed code against the same baseline; compare repeatable results before accepting an algorithmic claim.
assumptions: Transfer to the proposed workflow remains untested.

limitations: Evidence gap: these benchmark findings do not determine the quality of a particular vendor tool.

cases.evidence: The medical report system separately checked factual support and coverage of patient needs; clinicians preferred its responses in the study.

implications.text: The medical report system separately checked factual support and coverage of patient needs. This could inform separate accuracy and coverage checks for executive research briefs.
implications.suggested_action: Revise the brief-review checklist to assess factual support and coverage separately; ask subject-matter reviewers to identify unsupported claims and missing required points.
assumptions: Transfer to the proposed workflow remains untested.

limitations: Transfer gap: clinician preference in medical report interpretation does not establish executive brief quality.
